symbols.name: transformed axes
symbols.meaning: The number of transformed axes, d-1.
symbols.quote: Let $D=d-1$ be the number of transformed axes (a new meaning of $D$), and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_D)$.

symbols.name: leftover bits
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of an axis left over after whole K-bit chunks.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the bits of an axis left over after whole chunks (not a lowest bit), and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, the number of whole chunks per axis (not a sequence length), so $\ell-1=qK+b$.

symbols.name: whole chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of whole K-bit chunks per axis.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the bits of an axis left over after whole chunks (not a lowest bit), and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, the number of whole chunks per axis (not a sequence length), so $\ell-1=qK+b$.

symbols.name: layout permutation
symbols.meaning: The record permutation defined by the prefix moves and chunk exchanges.
symbols.quote: The moves and exchanges define the record permutation $L$ (not a linear map or a dimension loss); undoing them in reverse order gives $L^{-1}$.

symbols.name: bit reversal
symbols.meaning: The bit-reversal permutation applied along every axis.
symbols.quote: Write $B$ for bit reversal along every axis (not a row length), so the exact transforms are $BF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}$.

symbols.name: round input
symbols.quote: For the array $z$ entering a round (not a suffix), the layer returns $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$ and the next operation is the signed coefficient permutation $J_E$.

relations.quote: The layout keeps the bit-reversed output order of [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md).

derivations.quote: Call an axis long if it has $\ell$ address bits and short if $\ell-1$.
Move to a prefix, one slot at a time, the top bit of each long axis and the $b$ lowest bits of every axis. At most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ slots move so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$
Scan the target positions left to right, exchanging the chunk there with the required one if they differ: at most $Dq-1$ exchanges.
In a chunk round the selected bit has the same offset in $D$ consecutive chunks, so one layer performs it, at cost $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total
A prefix round processes its at most $D$ bits individually, each at $O(Tp)$, so $O(Tpd)$. At most $b+1\le K$ such rounds give $O(TpdK)$
Truncation toward zero is odd and acts separately on each real and imaginary part, so $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$: each round truncates once, after the exact contraction.

The contraction does not increase the norm of the difference between computed and exact arrays, and truncation moves each entry by less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$; the permutations in $L$ are isometries and add no error. From zero error the $\ell$ rounds leave error below $\sqrt2\,\ell\,2^{-p}$

The forward procedure moves records by $L$ first, so its exact operator is $(LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-L^{-1})L=LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$. The opposite procedure restores by $L^{-1}$ after its arithmetic, giving $L^{-1}(LF_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1})=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$.

The forward procedure moves records by $L$ first, so its exact operator is $(LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-L^{-1})L=LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$. The opposite procedure restores by $L^{-1}$ after its arithmetic, giving $L^{-1}(LF_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1})=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$.
